key=torch.tensor([[[[1.],[-1.]],[[3.],[-3.]]]])

name: scales feature dot products and keeps batches and query tokens separate
input: independent per-head oracle; multiple group sizes, noncontiguous inputs, dtypes, Tq != Tk
test:
import math
import torch
torch.manual_seed(367)
for dtype in (torch.float32,torch.float64):
    for hq,hkv in ((6,1),(6,2),(6,3),(3,3)):
        q=torch.randn(2,hq,2,8,dtype=dtype)[...,::2]
        k=torch.randn(2,hkv,3,8,dtype=dtype)[...,::2]
        v=torch.randn(2,hkv,3,8,dtype=dtype)[...,::2]
        before=[x.clone() for x in (q,k,v)]
        expected=torch.stack([torch.stack([(q[b,h]@k[b,h//(hq//hkv)].T/math.sqrt(4)).softmax(-1)@v[b,h//(hq//hkv)] for h in range(hq)]) for b in range(2)])
        actual=grouped_query_attention(q,k,v)
        assert isinstance(actual,torch.Tensor) and actual.shape==(2,hq,2,4)
        assert actual.dtype==dtype and actual.device==q.device
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual,expected,rtol=2e-5,atol=2e-6)
        assert all(torch.equal(x,old) for x,old in zip((q,k,v),before))
q,k,v=(x.tolist() for x in (q,k,v))
torch.testing.assert_close(grouped_query_attention(q,k,v),expected.float(),rtol=2e-5,atol=2e-6)

name: shared-KV gradients and device match an independent per-head oracle
input: every input receives accumulated gradients through shared KV heads
test:
import math
import torch
torch.manual_seed(368)
for device in (['cpu','cuda'] if torch.cuda.is_available() else ['cpu']):
    for hq,hkv in ((6,1),(6,2),(3,3)):
        q=torch.randn(2,hq,2,3,dtype=torch.float64,device=device,requires_grad=True)
        k=torch.randn(2,hkv,4,3,dtype=torch.float64,device=device,requires_grad=True)
        v=torch.randn(2,hkv,4,3,dtype=torch.float64,device=device,requires_grad=True)
        expected=torch.stack([torch.stack([(q[b,h]@k[b,h//(hq//hkv)].T/math.sqrt(3)).softmax(-1)@v[b,h//(hq//hkv)] for h in range(hq)]) for b in range(2)])
        actual=grouped_query_attention(q,k,v)
        assert actual.dtype==q.dtype and actual.device==q.device and actual.requires_grad
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual,expected)
        probe=torch.randn_like(expected)
        expected_grads=torch.autograd.grad((expected*probe).sum(),(q,k,v))
        actual_grads=torch.autograd.grad((actual*probe).sum(),(q,k,v))
        for a,e in zip(actual_grads,expected_grads): torch.testing.assert_close(a,e,rtol=1e-9,atol=1e-10)
